Ordered by concept, following the five patterns: each group starts one step beyond a solved problem and adds one idea at a time.

::: {.practice}
- [CF 363B · Fence](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/363/B){rating="1100"} — the fixed slide hunting a minimum, reporting where the window starts.
- [CF 1690D · Black and White Stripe](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1690/D){rating="1000"} — slide a count of white cells over every length-$k$ window.
- [LC 1456 · Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-number-of-vowels-in-a-substring-of-given-length/){difficulty="Medium"} — a counting fold instead of a sum.
- [CF 961B · Lecture Sleep](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/961/B){rating="1200"} — a base score plus the best fixed window of *extra* gain.
- [LC 1052 · Grumpy Bookstore Owner](https://leetcode.com/problems/grumpy-bookstore-owner/){difficulty="Medium"} — the same base-plus-window split.
- [CF 1692G · 2^Sort](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1692/G){rating="1400"} — turn the condition into a 0/1 array first, then count good fixed windows.
- [CF 1692E · Binary Deque](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1692/E){rating="1200"} — remove from both ends: the complement is the longest middle with a given sum.
- [LC 2516 · Take K of Each Character From Left and Right](https://leetcode.com/problems/take-k-of-each-character-from-left-and-right/){difficulty="Medium"} — the complement with a per-letter count budget.
- [LC 1493 · Longest Subarray of 1's After Deleting One Element](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-subarray-of-1s-after-deleting-one-element/){difficulty="Medium"} — the zero budget with $k = 1$.
- [CF 660C · Hard Process](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/660/C){rating="1600"} — the zero budget, plus printing the best window.
- [CF 676C · Vasya and String](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/676/C){rating="1500"} — the zero budget once for each of the two letters.
- [LC 424 · Longest Repeating Character Replacement](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-repeating-character-replacement/){difficulty="Medium"} — the budget is "cells that differ from the window's most common letter".
- [CF 1873F · Money Trees](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1873/F){rating="1300"} — a sum budget plus a rule that forces a restart.
- [CF 602B · Approximating a Constant Range](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/602/B){rating="1400"} — longest window with max minus min at most 1, from a count table.
- [CF 1354B · Ternary String](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1354/B){rating="1200"} — the shortest window containing all three characters.
- [CF 701C · They Are Everywhere](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/701/C){rating="1500"} — the shortest window containing every distinct value.
- [LC 1234 · Replace the Substring for Balanced String](https://leetcode.com/problems/replace-the-substring-for-balanced-string/){difficulty="Medium"} — shortest window whose *outside* satisfies the rule.
- [LC 76 · Minimum Window Substring](https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-window-substring/){difficulty="Hard"} — shortest cover with a need/have table; the string chapters return to it.
- [LC 2302 · Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-subarrays-with-score-less-than-k/){difficulty="Hard"} — the `r - l + 1` batch for a sum-times-length score.
- [CF 1736C1 · Good Subarrays (Easy Version)](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1736/C1){rating="1300"} — a position-dependent rule that is still shrink-safe.
- [LC 1248 · Count Number of Nice Subarrays](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-number-of-nice-subarrays/){difficulty="Medium"} — exactly $k$ odd numbers by the at-most difference.
- [LC 930 · Binary Subarrays With Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-subarrays-with-sum/){difficulty="Medium"} — exact sum on 0/1 values: at-most difference or prefix map.
- [CF 165C · Another Problem on Strings](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/165/C){rating="1600"} — exactly $k$ ones, including $k = 0$.
- [LC 1695 · Maximum Erasure Value](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-erasure-value/){difficulty="Medium"} — the all-distinct table on a longest window, scored by sum.
- [LC 438 · Find All Anagrams in a String](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-all-anagrams-in-a-string/){difficulty="Medium"} — a fixed window whose table must match a target table.
- [LC 2841 · Maximum Sum of Almost Unique Subarray](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-sum-of-almost-unique-subarray/){difficulty="Medium"} — a fixed window needing at least $m$ distinct values.

- [LC 2537 · Count the Number of Good Subarrays](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-the-number-of-good-subarrays/){difficulty="Medium"} — `n - r` again, with a pair count maintained from the table.
- [LC 1838 · Frequency of the Most Frequent Element](https://leetcode.com/problems/frequency-of-the-most-frequent-element/){difficulty="Medium"} — sort first, then a sum-budget window: the bridge to @sec-srt.
- [LC 862 · Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K](https://leetcode.com/problems/shortest-subarray-with-sum-at-least-k/){difficulty="Hard"} — negatives: where the window ends and prefix sums with a monotone deque begin.
:::

## Further reading

- [Competitive Programmer's Handbook (Laaksonen)](https://cses.fi/book/book.pdf) — chapter 8, "Amortized analysis": § 8.1 is the two pointers method with the subarray-sum example and the amortised bound of @sec-sw-a2; § 8.3 is the sliding window minimum that @sec-sw-a5 hands off to.
- [USACO Guide — Two Pointers](https://usaco.guide/silver/two-pointers) — the same-direction two-pointer technique with graded contest problems; pairs with Patterns 2 and 3.
- [USACO Guide — Sliding Window](https://usaco.guide/gold/sliding-window) — fixed windows with a data structure inside (sets, the monotone deque), the next step after @sec-sw-p5.
- [CP-Algorithms — Minimum stack / Minimum queue](https://cp-algorithms.com/data_structures/stack_queue_modification.html) — how to keep the minimum of a queue in $O(1)$ amortised, which answers window minima: the case a running fold cannot handle.
- [GeeksforGeeks — Sliding Window Technique](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/window-sliding-technique/) — a beginner's walk through fixed and variable windows with many short worked examples, useful as a second explanation of @sec-sw-a1 and @sec-sw-a2.
- [Wikipedia — Amortized analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amortized_analysis) — the aggregate, accounting and potential methods; the aggregate method is exactly the "each pointer moves at most $n$ times" proof.
- [Python `collections` documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html) — `Counter`, `defaultdict` and `deque`, the three containers this chapter's windows carry.
